decisions.title: Building regulations
decisions.situation: You stack three blocks. For a moment, the tower stands. Then you discover what your elbow has been planning.

choices.label: Build it again with a wider bottom
Knock down the next tower on purpose
Line the blocks up on the floor

result.title: A better foundation
result.body: The new tower survives your elbow. Your hand brings it down a little later.

journal.text: I rebuilt a block tower with a wider base.

decisions.title: Permanent exhibition
decisions.situation: You draw a huge purple person on the wall. Giulia walks in while you are adding the teeth.

choices.label: Show off your work
Help clean it up
Blame a very tall baby

result.title: Mixed reviews
result.body: Giulia gives you paper. The wall gets a long scrub.

journal.text: I drew a purple person on the wall. It was not a commissioned piece.

decisions.title: A very close race
decisions.situation: Your shadow keeps reaching the wall before you. You try standing still. It has apparently thought of that too.

choices.label: Make it do a silly dance
Move closer to the light
Sit down beside it

result.title: An obedient rival
result.body: You stop trying to beat the shadow and give it increasingly ridiculous instructions.

journal.text: I made my shadow do a silly dance.

decisions.title: Imaginary friend wanted
decisions.situation: Giulia is alone at break. They say their imaginary friend has moved to a better school. They are interviewing replacements on the empty part of the bench.

choices.label: Help interview the invisible applicants
Apply, despite being inconveniently real
Pretend you have accidentally sat on one

result.title: A crowded bench
result.body: You reject the first applicant for imaginary biting. Giulia rejects the second for actually being a dragon. You run out of break before making an appointment.

journal.text: I helped Giulia interview replacements for an imaginary friend.

decisions.title: Hotel living room
decisions.situation: You ask Giulia whether you can camp in the living room. Your packing list contains six cushions and no clothes.

choices.label: Help make a proper sleeping spot
Ask Giulia to camp too
Decide your bed is better

result.title: Room with a sofa
result.body: Giulia helps you set up, then checks on you before bed.

journal.text: I camped in the living room with Giulia’s help.

decisions.title: Nobody told the spy
decisions.situation: You catch Giulia explaining your secret code to everyone. They claim it is fine because they have invented a second, more secret code. You have not been told it.

choices.label: Demand to inspect the new codebook
Invent a silent signal for “you are fired”
Tell everyone the first code means nothing

result.title: One unhelpful entry
result.body: The new codebook contains one word: “banana”. Giulia says its meaning is classified. You add a second word meaning “tell your partner things”.

journal.text: I inspected Giulia’s replacement secret code and found one word.

decisions.title: Hostile snack takeover
decisions.situation: Giulia offers a plain cracker for your favourite snack. They call the cracker “rare”. There are twelve more in the packet.

choices.label: Demand two snacks for your one
Eat your snack during the sales pitch
Split yours and spare the cracker

result.title: The negotiator gets greedy
result.body: Giulia nearly agrees, then notices you smiling. They withdraw the cracker and their goodwill.

journal.text: I tried to turn Giulia’s snack offer into a better deal for myself.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Giulia one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Stop before they can demonstrate
Agree on one round each, then stop
Demand rematches until you win

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Giulia seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Giulia I would.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Giulia whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them
Help make a short apology
Add microwave sound effects

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Giulia said anything worse.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Giulia finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Watch it together
Ask to keep the recording private
Defend the bath theory

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Giulia remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Giulia.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Giulia secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Make them delete the recording
Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Giulia deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Giulia delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: The pancake is on the ceiling
decisions.situation: You help Giulia make “foolproof” pancakes. The first one is stuck to the ceiling. Neither of you wants to discuss how it got there.

choices.label: Consult the recipe before pancake two
Ask Giulia to demonstrate
Attempt the exact same toss again

result.title: The pan is a serving suggestion
result.body: The instructions recommend turning it gently. You complete the next batch without adding anything else to the ceiling.

journal.text: I read the recipe after a disastrous pancake toss with Giulia.

decisions.title: Do teenagers smell fear?
decisions.situation: Giulia asks you to fix their phone. An open draft says, “Do teenagers smell fear? Mine only appears when the fridge opens.” They suddenly offer to fix it themselves.

choices.label: Offer an answer from a qualified teenager
Fix it without mentioning the draft
Send their contacts a mocking reading of it

result.title: Mostly, we smell cheese
result.body: Giulia laughs and admits they were having a moan. You fix the phone, then both turn towards the sound of the fridge opening.

journal.text: I caught Giulia complaining about me and answered their question about teenagers.

decisions.title: A reminder that needs reminding
decisions.situation: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
Work backwards from the context
Assume it will make sense later

result.title: Future you gets better information
result.body: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.

journal.text: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: The important businessman
decisions.situation: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
Offer them the chair after your drink
Explain that reserving chairs is bad business

result.title: A volatile juice market
result.body: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.

journal.text: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing
Send someone a proper message
Investigate another hour of success

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

choices.label: Ask what the label means
Step back and let them stop it
Ask whether smoke costs extra

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Rome offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
Cover the portrait and leave

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

result.title: Medical care arranged

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

Let your attention rest
Check the same screen again

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

Leave before the eulogy

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
Follow the tour without breaking eye contact

result.title: New evidence
result.body: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.

journal.text: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in Rome.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

Perform an increasingly furious dance

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Giulia also confessed to approving the haircut.

result.title: A review they can use

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.
